entities.text:
High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan Bench At
 Jaipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
1. Petitioner has filed this miscellaneous petition aggrieved by order dated 25.09.2013, passed by Sessions Judge, Jhunjhunu, in Criminal Revision No. 84/2013, whereby the revision petition preferred by the petitioner was dismissed and order dated 12.08.2013, whereby the charge has been framed against the accused-petitioner under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954 was upheld.
2.
It is contended by counsel for the petitioner that petitioner is a dealer, his case is similar to that of the retailer who has been discharged as per the Act.

It is contended that as per Sub-Section 2 of Section 19 vendor shall not be deem to have committed an offence pertaining to the sale of any adulterated food, if he proves (2 of 3) [CRLMP-1405/2014] that article of food while in his possession was stored and that it was sold in the same state as he purchased it.
3.

It is further contended that this benefit has been given to the retailer, but has not been given to the petitioner as the petitioner at that relevant time was unable to produce the bills vide which he has purchased the "Ghee".

It is contended that the petitioner be given an opportunity to produce the original bills before the concerned Court and the concerned Court be directed now to reconsider the prayer of the petitioner with regard to the framing of charge.
4.
I have considered the contentions of the petitioner at the time when the Court decided the matter on 25.07.2013.

It was established by the retailer that he has received the consignment in the same Vinod Kumar vs State Of Rajasthan And Anr on 7 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174640662/
1 condition and therefore, he was given the benefit of Section 19 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

entities.text: Vinod Kumar vs State Of Rajasthan And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The present petitioner was unable to establish that he has received the consignment in the same condition and has sent to the retailer in the same condition in which it was received by him.
Consequently, the Court below rejected the prayer of the petitioner and framed the charges against him.

5. The petitioner has availed the remedy of revision and the revision stands dismissed.
6.

Sub-Clause 2 of Section 19 provides that if a vendor proves that he has purchased the article of food from a distributor or dealer with warranty in the prescribed form and the article of food while in his possession was properly stored and he sold it in the same state as he purchased it, then he deem to any offence.

7. The present petitioner has got some bills to establish the sale from the manufacturer, but now after framing of the charge that stage is not available and even as per Sub-Section 2 of Section 19 it is for him to prove before the Court that he received the goods from the manufacturer with a warranty and has remained with him in the same state in which he received from the manufacturer.
8. Since the petitioner was not able to establish the same before the Trial Court and the Court has framed charge which has also been upheld by the Revisional Court, there being a Bar of second revision and petitioner having availed of the remedy of revision, at this stage it cannot be held that petitioner has been wrongly charged therefore, I am not inclined to entertain the miscellaneous petition.
9. The criminal miscellaneous petition is accordingly dismissed.
The stay petition also stands disposed of.

(PANKAJ BHANDARI)J. Amit/4 Vinod Kumar vs State Of Rajasthan And Anr on 7 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174640662/
